quote: This is, this is Bucky with Ion. I'm reaching out about the solar for me for the online.
stewart_read: The intro is stumbled and garbled, weakening the legitimacy anchor even though a company name and lead-source reference are technically present.
coaching_implication: Slow down the open — state name, company, and lead source cleanly before moving to questions.

quote: Oh, well, then I don't qualify because that's under a 100.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a low-bill anchor framed as disqualifying; rep reassures generically instead of flipping it into forward motion or curiosity about savings.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have believed a brief reassurance was sufficient since the qualifier itself isn't a hard bill floor.
coaching_implication: Use the low bill as a hook — ask what she'd want to see before assuming it rules her out, rather than just saying 'you're still fine.'

quote: I'm not putting anything on a flat roof.
stewart_read: This is a non-standard roof scenario (flat roof, no ground mount offered) that the rep resolves alone in real time instead of checking with a supervisor or exploring options.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be correct that Ion never does ground mount, in which case confirming quickly is appropriate; but no attempt was made to verify or explore mounting alternatives.
coaching_implication: On non-standard roof types, pause and confirm current install options before conceding the deal is dead.

quote: What utility oh, wait. You already said that. Kit Carson?
stewart_read: Rep re-asks a question already answered, signaling disorganization and eroding the conversational flow.
coaching_implication: Track what's already been captured within the call to avoid re-asking and appearing scattered.

quote: No. No. No. No. This is wide open sagebrush.
stewart_read: Customer reacts defensively to a perceived doubt about her home; rep clarifies but doesn't use the moment to build rapport or pivot smoothly into the next qualifier.
alternative_hypothesis: This may be a minor friction point rather than a true objection since the customer immediately cooperates afterward.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge quickly and move on with confidence rather than repeating 'no, no, no' defensively back.

quote: My highest electric bill has been $75,
stewart_read: Bill captured but at a low figure and never reflected back or leveraged before the call ends on the roof gate.
coaching_implication: Even a low bill can be flipped ('even at $75 there's still an offset opportunity') — capture alone did nothing here.
